newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Two Timorese detained for beating journalist.
newsitem.headline: Two Timorese detained for beating journalist.

text.p: Two East Timorese have been detained for an attack on a local journalist in the territory's capital of Dili at the weekend, police said on Tuesday.
"Two people have been detained," East Timor's deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone from Dili.
He said police were still searching for six other youths involved in the attack. He gave no further details.
Gaudensius Mao, an East Timor correspondent for the Jakarta-based Tiras magazine, was beaten unconscious by eight youths on Sunday night.
On Tuesday the official Antara news agency quoted Mao, who was hospitalised after the attack, as saying the youths mistook him for an Indonesian intelligence officer.

Many East Timorese do not accept the rule of Indonesia, which invaded the eastern half of the island in 1975 and annexed it as its 27th province the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Police in East Timor said it was too early to speculate on a motive for the attack.
In August, a Yogyakarta-based reporter with the Bernas daily, known for his critical reporting of local government affairs, was beaten to death by an unidentified attacker.
Both the official National Commission on Human Rights and officials of the Indonesian Journalists' Association have questioned whether the police conducted a proper investigation.
They have said evidence suggests the man arrested by police as the suspect was not the murderer.
